title: Complex multiplication
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Kronecker's first limit formula
modules.note:
`New.kronecker_limit` computes the first two terms at `s = 1` of the Epstein zeta function of a
lattice in `ℂ`, in terms of its area and of the discriminant `g₂³ - 27 g₃²`. The Epstein function is
not continued analytically: only real `s` with `1 < s < 2` occur, and a right derivative at `1`.

For the lattice `ℤ τ + ℤ`, each row `∑ n, |m τ + n|^(-2s)` with `m ≥ 1` is compared with the
integral `∫ |m τ + t|^(-2s) dt` (`New.hasSum_shiftedTerm`). The errors `New.meanError` sum to a
function continuous on `[1, 2]`, the integrals to a multiple of `ζ(2s - 1)`, which has a simple pole
at 1. At `s = 1` the cotangent series expresses the errors through `log |∏ (1 - q ^ n)|`
(`New.tsum_meanError_one`).

Notions from other files:
* `PeriodPair.area`: The area |Im(ω̄₁ω₂)| of the fundamental parallelogram spanned by the periods
  ω₁, ω₂ of a period pair.
modules.literature:
Known result: Kronecker's first limit formula. Here the real limit from the right is proved for any
lattice and stated with the discriminant. Rows are compared with integrals by the mean value
theorem. Source: C. L. Siegel, Lectures on Advanced Analytic Number Theory (1961), Chapter I,
Theorem 1; for a proof of this shape, F. Chamizo, A simple evaluation of a theta value, the
Kronecker limit formula and a formula of Ramanujan, Ramanujan J. (2022), Prop. 3.1.

modules.title: CM lattices as multiples of fractional ideals, and good reduction of CM curves
modules.note:
Let `K = ℚ(√-d) ⊂ ℂ` (`New.QuadField`), where `d` is a prime `≡ 7 mod 8` (`New.PrimeSevenModEight`).
We show that the lattice of every datum `New.CMLattice d` is a multiple `u 𝔞` of a fractional ideal
of `K` and that every ideal gives one, and we compute the covolumes. We then follow isogenies of
degree two through the class group. This shows that the discriminant of a CM lattice, normalised by
`℘''(t) = 2`, is a unit at every prime, as it is for a curve with good reduction.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.latticeModule`: the lattice of a datum as an `𝓞 K`-module;
  `New.QuadField.scaledIdeal`: `(u, 𝔞) ↦ u 𝔞`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_latticeModule_eq_scaledIdeal`: the lattice of every datum has the form
  `u 𝔞`.
* `New.QuadField.exists_cmLattice_latticeModule_eq_scaledIdeal`: every `𝔞` has a multiple `u 𝔞` that
  is the lattice of a datum.
* `New.QuadField.area_eq_of_eq_scaledIdeal`: the covolume of `u 𝔞` is `|u|² N(𝔞) √d / 2`.
* `PeriodPair.IsOrderTwo.scaledDisc_sum_prod`, `PeriodPair.IsOrderTwo.scaledDisc_mul_of_isogeny`:
  identities for the discriminants `s(u)` of a lattice scaled to `℘''(u) = 2` at the points `u` of
  order two.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_scaledDisc_le_one`, `New.CMLattice.prod_scaledDisc_t`: for a family of data,
  one in each ideal class, the numbers `s(u)` are integral, and those at the points `t` have the
  product `±1`.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_disc_eq_one`: the discriminant `a₁⁴ - 64` of a CM lattice is a unit at every
  prime.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMLattice d`: a period lattice `Λ` stable under `𝓞 K`, with a point `t` of order two and a
  number `a₁`.
* `PeriodPair.area`: the area `|Im(ω̄₁ω₂)|` of the fundamental parallelogram spanned by the periods
  `ω₁`, `ω₂` of a period pair.
modules.literature:
Known result: lattices stable under `𝓞 K` are the multiples of fractional ideals. Source: Silverman,
Advanced topics in the arithmetic of elliptic curves.

Known result: Siegel units. For a torsion point `u`, the twelfth power of Klein's form at `u` times
the discriminant is an algebraic integer, and a unit if two different primes of `K` divide the
annihilator of `u`. The file proves the case of the point `t`, whose annihilator is `(2)`; there the
number is the discriminant `a₁⁴ - 64`. Source: Kubert, Lang, Modular Units. Up to sign the numbers
`s(u)` are the 24-th powers of Weber's functions. Source: Birch, Weber's class invariants, 1969.

modules.title: Galois conjugates of CM curves: conjugate sections, isogenies and translates of θ
modules.note:
Let `σ` be a field automorphism of `ℂ`, and let `C`, `C'` be CM data (`New.CMLattice`) with
`C'.a₁ = σ C.a₁`, so that their cubics y² + a₁xy = x³ + x are conjugate under `σ`. Write `θ`, `θ'`
for their theta functions, and `New.taylorVia σ f` for the Taylor series of `f` at 0 with `σ`
applied to its coefficients. The bare letter `σ` is the automorphism, while `C.σ` is the sigma
function of the lattice of `C`. For `σ ∈ Aut(ℂ/K)` with `K = ℚ(√-d)` (`quadInt d` is the image of
`𝓞_K` in `ℂ`, fixed by `σ`), a conjugate CM datum exists, and conjugation extends to isogenies and
to translates of `θ`; this is a step towards `New.CMLattice.complex_multiplication_theta`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.thetaQuotient`: the quotient `θ' / σ θ` of power series, by which the theta functions differ.
* `New.taylorAtZero_monomialSection`, `New.exists_conjugate_section`: monomial sections, and hence
  all sections `f` of degree `m` of `C`, have conjugates with Taylor series `(θ' / σ θ) ^ m * σ f`;
  the second lemma transports points as well.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_galConjugate_of_g₂_g₃`, `New.CMLattice.galConjugate`: a lattice with the
  invariants `σ g₂`, `σ g₃` carries a CM datum with the number `σ a₁`, and one such datum is chosen.
* `New.CMLattice.thetaQuotient_eq_one`, `New.CMLattice.taylorAtZero_theta_eq_taylorVia`: for a CM
  datum `D` with invariant `σ a₁`, the Taylor series of the theta function is the conjugate of that
  of `θ`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_taylorVia_twistedTranslate_theta`: when the lattice of `C` is `Ω 𝓞_K` and
  `S` is a finite subset of `K`, there is a period `v` of `D` such that, for all `s ∈ S`, the Taylor
  series of the translate by `s v` of the theta function of `D` is the conjugate of that of the
  translate of `θ` by `s Ω`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMLattice.θ`: The twisted translate (`twistedTranslate 1 u f` is
  `z ↦ exp(−π(zū + |u|²/2)/area Λ) f(z + u)`) of the sigma function `C.σ` by the point t of order
  two, normalised to 1 at 0; it vanishes exactly on t + Λ.
* `New.CMLattice.translatedX`, `New.CMLattice.translatedY`: The coordinates x(z) = ℘(z + t) − ℘(t)
  and y(z) = ½(℘′(z + t) − a₁x(z)) of the curve.
* `New.CMLattice.sections`: The sections of degree m: theta functions for the lattice Λ with
  hermitian form mH and multiplier χ^m, for the hermitian form H and multiplier χ of `θ`.
* `PeriodPair.IsIsogeny`: L.IsIsogeny M a N says that a maps the periods of L to those of M and that
  a·ā·area(L) = N·area(M).
* `New.CMLattice.monomialSection`: For j = (a, b, c), the section θ^a·(C.σ²)^b·G^c of degree
  a + 2b + 3c, with C.σ the sigma function and G = `New.CMLattice.translatedYThetaCube`.
modules.literature:
Part of a known result: Main theorem of complex multiplication for elliptic curves, soft form. See
`Lib.CM.ChowlaSelberg`. No reciprocity law is used: the conjugate lattice comes from uniformisation,
and points are matched by transporting sections.

modules.title: Finitely many CM lattices
modules.note:
* `New.CMLattice.finite_range_latticeModule`: for a prime `d ≡ 7 mod 8`, only finitely many lattices
  in `ℂ` underlie a CM lattice for `K = ℚ(√-d)`.
* `New.CMLattice.theta_eq_of_latticeModule_eq`: the theta function `θ` depends only on the lattice;
  in particular it does not depend on the representative `t` of the point of order two.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_norm_twistedTranslate_theta_le`: the values `(T_u θ)(0)` are bounded
  uniformly in the CM lattice and in `u`.

Each CM lattice is a multiple of one of finitely many ideals, and the scaling `℘''(t) = 2` fixes the
factor up to a fourth root of unity.

Notions from other files:
* `C : CMLattice d`: a lattice `C.Λ` in `ℂ` stable under `𝓞_K`, with a point `C.t` of order two
  modulo `C.Λ` such that neither `ω t` nor `ω̄ t` lies in `C.Λ` (`ω = quadGen d = (1 + √-d) / 2`),
  scaled so that `℘''(C.t) = 2`.
* `C.latticeModule`: the lattice `C.Λ` as an `𝓞_K`-submodule of `ℂ`.
* `QuadField.scaledIdeal d (u, 𝔞)`: the submodule `u 𝔞` of `ℂ`, for a fractional ideal `𝔞` of `K`.
* `C.twistedTranslate 1 u f`: the function `(T_u f)(z) = exp(-π (z ū + |u|² / 2) / C.area)
  f(z + u)`.
* `C.θ`: the translate `T_t σ` of the sigma function, normalised to `1` at `0`.
modules.literature:
Known result: lattices with complex multiplication by `𝓞_K` up to homothety correspond to the ideal
classes. Source: Silverman, Advanced topics in the arithmetic of elliptic curves, Chapter II.

modules.title: Odd class number, ζ_K = ζ·L(s, χ), theta functions with CM and Chowla–Selberg
modules.note:
Throughout, `K = ℚ(√-d)` (`New.QuadField d`) for a prime `d ≡ 7 mod 8` (`New.PrimeSevenModEight d`),
and `χ` is the Legendre symbol modulo `d`. For such `K` the class number is odd, and the Dedekind
zeta function factors as `ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, χ)`. The second part treats curves with complex
multiplication by `K`, given by CM lattices `C : New.CMLattice d`. For these curves the file proves
a complex multiplication law for the translates of the theta function when the lattice is `Ω₀ 𝓞_K`,
and the formula of Chowla and Selberg for the areas of the conjugate lattices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.QuadField.classGroup_sq_bijective`: squaring permutes the class group, that is, the class
  number is odd.
* `New.QuadField.eulerProd_one_eq_zeta_mul`: `ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, χ)` for real `s > 1`, with `χ` the
  Legendre symbol modulo `d`.
* `New.CMLattice.IsComplexMultiplicationData`, `New.CMLattice.complex_multiplication_theta`: the
  action of `σ` on the translates of `θ` by torsion points is given by one finite adele of `K`, if
  the lattice is `Ω₀ 𝓞_K`.
* `New.CMLattice.sum_kronecker_terms`: Kronecker's limit formula summed over the class group.
* `New.CMLattice.chowla_selberg`: after scaling by the conjugates of one unit, all conjugate
  lattices have the area that this sum gives.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMLattice`: A lattice `Λ` stable under the integers of `ℚ(√-d)`, with a point `t` of order
  two modulo `Λ` such that `ω t`, `ω̄ t ∉ Λ` for `ω = (1 + √-d) / 2`, scaled so that `℘''(t) = 2`,
  and a square root `a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`; the discriminant of `Λ` is `a₁⁴ - 64`.
* `New.CMLattice.θ`: The twisted translate of the sigma function by `t`, normalised to `1` at `0`.
* `PeriodPair.area`: The area |Im(ω̄₁ω₂)| of the fundamental parallelogram spanned by the periods
  ω₁, ω₂ of a period pair.
* `New.chowlaSelbergConst`: The real number `γ - Re L'/L(1, χ_K)`, with `γ` Euler's constant.
modules.literature:
Known result: The class number of an imaginary quadratic field of prime discriminant is odd. Here it
is stated as bijectivity of squaring on the class group, for primes congruent to 7 modulo 8. Source:
C. F. Gauss, Disquisitiones; D. Cox, Primes of the form x²+ny² (1989), §3 and §6.

Known result: The Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field is the product of the Riemann zeta
function and the L-function of its character, and the sum of the zeta functions of its ideal
classes. Source: J. Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory (1999), VII.5 and VII.10.

Known result: The formula of Lerch and of Chowla and Selberg for the geometric mean of
area · |disc|^(1/6) over the ideal classes (`New.CMLattice.sum_kronecker_terms`). Here the
discriminant is prime with 2 split, and the mean is left in terms of the logarithmic derivative of
the L-function at 1, with no Gamma values. The integrality of isogenies then gives one number, a
unit at every p-adic place, whose conjugates scale all conjugate lattices to this area. Source: A.
Selberg, S. Chowla, On Epstein's zeta-function, J. reine angew. Math. 227 (1967) 86-110; B. Gross,
On the periods of abelian varieties, arXiv 2005.04194.

Known result: The main theorem of complex multiplication for elliptic curves, without the
reciprocity law. It is shown that the conjugate lattice is `Ω 𝔠² / N(𝔠)` and that one finite adele
describes the Galois action on the translates of the theta function by torsion points. The adele is
not identified with the Artin map and is not shown here to be a unit. Source: G. Shimura,
Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions (1971), Thm 5.4; J. Milne, Complex
Multiplication (2020), 9.17.

modules.title: Integral series rings 𝔬[[T]], congruence parts of power series, a functional equation
modules.group: The formal group of a CM curve
modules.note:
Let `𝔬` (`New.valRingCp p`) be the valuation ring of `ℂ_[p]`, and let `𝔬[[X]]` be the range of the
inclusion `New.seriesToCp` into `ℂ_[p]⟦X⟧`. For a series `T = X + ⋯`, the file studies the ring
`𝔬[[T]]` of integral series in `T`. For the coordinate `y` of a CM curve, it shows that `𝔬[[y]]`
contains `x` and is stable under `d/dz`. It then treats the part of a series in the degrees of one
class mod `m`, and the integrality of the solutions of a functional equation `Y(π z) = π G(Y)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsSeriesGenerator A T`: the series `T = X + ⋯` generates `A`, that is, `A = 𝔬[[T]]`. Such a
  ring is closed under integral scalars. It is closed under `f ↦ f(a X)` when it contains `T(a X)`.
  Its elements whose constant term has norm `1` are invertible. Any series `f = X + ⋯` in `A`
  generates it too (`New.IsSeriesGenerator.of_mem`).
* `New.CMLattice.integralSeriesRing C`: the ring `𝔬[[y]]`. Here `y` (`New.CMLattice.translatedY`)
  and `x` (`New.CMLattice.translatedX`) are the coordinates of the CM curve `y² + a₁ x y = x³ + x`.
  `New.taylorVia ιₚ f` is the Taylor series of `f` at `0` with the p-adic place `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`
  applied to the coefficients.
* `New.CMLattice.taylorVia_translatedX_mem_integralSeriesRing`,
  `New.CMLattice.derivative_mem_integralSeriesRing`: `𝔬[[y]]` contains `x` and is stable under
  `d/dz`.
* `New.congruencePart_eq_sum`: for `m ≠ 0`, the part of a series in the degrees of one class mod `m`
  is a mean over the `m`-th roots of unity; `New.congruencePart_subst`: taking it commutes with the
  substitution of a series `T` with `T(0) = 0` that has only degrees `≡ 1` mod `m`.
* `New.exists_seriesToCp_eq_of_rescale_eq`: for `0 < |π| < 1`, `q > 1` and `E` integral of order at
  least two, a solution `Y = z + ⋯` of `Y(π z) / π = Y - Y ^ q + π E(Y)` is integral, by induction
  on the degree (`New.mem_range_seriesToCp_of_rescale_eq_X_sub_X_pow`), and `Y - Y ^ q ≡ z` modulo
  `π` (`New.C_dvd_sub_pow_sub_X_of_rescale_eq`).
* `New.dvd_coeff_sub_of_C_dvd_sub_pow_sub_X`: let `π` be a non-unit dividing `p` and `q > 1` a power
  of `p`. If `Y(0) = 0` and `Y - Y ^ q ≡ z` modulo `π`, then `Y ≡ ∑ z ^ q ^ j` modulo `π`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMLattice d`: a lattice `Λ` stable under the integers of `ℚ(√-d)`, with a point `t` of order
  two modulo `Λ` such that `ω t`, `ω̄ t ∉ Λ` for `ω = (1 + √-d) / 2`, scaled so that `℘''(t) = 2`,
  and a square root `a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`.
* `New.PrimeSevenModEight d`: the number `d` is a prime congruent to `7` modulo `8`.
modules.literature:
Known result: elementary facts on power series; the induction is that of the functional equation of
a Lubin–Tate group. Source: Lubin–Tate, Formal complex multiplication in local fields.

The statements on the CM curve use only that `a₁` is integral; `x ∈ 𝔬[[y]]` is Hensel's lemma for
the cubic.

modules.title: Notation at a prime, and elements of prime-power norm at split primes
modules.group: The formal group of a CM curve
modules.note:
For primes `p` and `d ≡ 7 mod 8`, the file defines the numbers and sets of exponents attached to `p`
and the imaginary quadratic field `K = ℚ(√-d)`, and computes them when `p` is split, inert or
ramified. For a prime `p` that splits in `K`, it then finds an element whose norm is a power of `p`
and whose conjugate is a unit at the `p`-adic place.

The statements use the following notions, for primes `p` and `d`; from `piPrime_mem_quadInt` on,
`d ≡ 7 mod 8` is assumed, and `quadInt d` is the ring of integers of `K` inside `ℂ`.

* `chiK d p`: the Legendre symbol `(p / d)`; for `d ≡ 7 mod 8` it is `1`, `-1`, `0` when `p` is
  split, inert, ramified in `K`.
* `primeNorm d p`, also written `q_p`: `p ^ 2` if `(p / d) = -1`, and `p` otherwise.
* `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]`: the embedding given by an instance `PadicPlace p`; the valuation `v` of
  `ℂ_[p]` with `v(p) = 1` is expressed by `‖x‖ = p ^ (-v(x))`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.piPrime`, `New.piPrimeValuation`: the number `π_p`, which is `√-d` for `p = d` and `p`
  otherwise, and its valuation `v(π_p)`, which is `1 / 2` for `p = d` and `1` otherwise.
* `New.varpiValuation`, `New.gammaPrime`: the numbers `ρ_p = v(π_p) / (q_p - 1)` and
  `γ_p = 1 / (p - 1) - ρ_p`.
* `New.partnerExponents`, `New.positivePartnerExponents`: the sets `I_p°` and `I_p`. The set `I_p°`
  consists of the odd numbers if `p` is inert, of all numbers if `p = d`, and is empty if `p`
  splits; `I_p` consists of its positive elements.
* `New.hasSum_gammaPrime`: `γ_p = v(π_p) ∑_{e ∈ I_p} p⁻ᵉ`.
* `New.piPrime_mul_conj`, `New.norm_piPrime`, `New.norm_piPrime_eq_rpow_pow`: the norm of `π_p` at a
  non-split prime, its valuation, and the relation `v(π_p) = (q_p - 1) ρ_p`.
* `New.exists_mul_conj_eq_pow`: for a prime `p` that splits in `K` there is an `α` in the ring of
  integers with `α ᾱ` a positive power of `p` and `ᾱ` a `p`-adic unit; the proof takes a generator
  of a power of the prime of `K` induced by the `p`-adic place.
modules.literature:
Known result: decomposition of primes in `ℚ(√-d)` and elements of prime-power norm at split primes.
The existence of `α` follows from the finiteness of the class group. The numbers `ρ_p`, `γ_p` and
the sets of exponents are notation, and the sum for `γ_p` is a geometric series.

modules.title: The inseparable degree
modules.group: The formal group of a CM curve
modules.note:
For `α ∈ 𝒪_K` let `o(α)` be the order in `y` of `y(α z) ∈ 𝒪[[y]]` modulo the maximal ideal of `𝒪`.

* `New.CMLattice.insepDegree_le`: `o(α) ≤ α ᾱ` for `α ≠ 0`, since `x(α z)` is, up to a unit, an
  integral polynomial in `x` with a unit coefficient in a degree at most `α ᾱ`.
* `New.CMLattice.insepDegree_piPrime_le`: `o(π_p) ≤ q_p` for every prime `p`.

## Notation

* `C : CMLattice d` is a lattice `Λ` stable under `𝒪_K = quadInt d`, the ring of integers of
  `K = ℚ(√-d)` in `ℂ`, with a point `t = C.t` of order two modulo `Λ`.
* `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` is the chosen place, `𝒪 = valRingCp p` is the valuation ring of `ℂ_[p]`, and
  `seriesToCp` is the inclusion `𝒪[[X]] → ℂ_[p][[X]]`.
* `taylorVia ιₚ f` is the Taylor series of `f` at `0` with `ιₚ` applied to its coefficients.
* `x` and `y` are the series of `C.translatedX` and `C.translatedY`, the coordinates of the curve
  `y ^ 2 + a₁ x y = x ^ 3 + x` at `z + t`, and `C.integralSeriesRing` is the ring `𝒪[[y]]`; `σ` is
  the sigma function of `Λ` and `θ = C.θ` its normalised twisted translate by `t`, with `θ(0) = 1`
  and `σ ^ 2 = x θ ^ 2`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the inseparable degree of the reduction of an isogeny is at most its degree. This
gives the bound on the height of the formal group in Deuring's criterion. Sources: Deuring, Die
Typen der Multiplikatorenringe elliptischer Funktionenkörper; Blake, A Deuring criterion for abelian
varieties, arXiv 1311.5454, Theorem 1.1; Bluher, Formal groups, elliptic curves, and some theorems
of Couveignes, ANTS-III, LNCS 1423 (1998), 3.2 and 6.1 (numbering of arXiv math/9708215).

modules.title: The formal parameter
modules.group: The formal group of a CM curve
modules.note:
Let `d ≡ 7` mod `8` be a prime and `C` a lattice with complex multiplication by the integers of
`K = ℚ(√-d)`. Let `p` be a prime, `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` a fixed embedding and `𝒪` the valuation ring of
`ℂ_[p]`. Power series are in the variable `z`, which is `X` in the code; so the formal parameter is
written `T`.

* `New.CMLattice.isSeriesGenerator_formalParam`: the part `T` of `y` in degrees `≡ 1` mod `q - 1`
  generates `𝒪[[y]]`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_scaled_formalParam`: for some `ϖ` of valuation `ρ_p` the series
  `Y = T(ϖ z) / ϖ` is integral, and `Y - Y ^ q ≡ z`, `Y ≡ ∑ z ^ q ^ j` mod `π_p`. The proof writes
  `T(π_p z) = π_p T + b₁ T ^ q + ⋯` with a unit `b₁` and takes `ϖ ^ (q - 1) = -π_p / b₁`.
* `New.CMLattice.rescale_mem_range_seriesToCp`, `New.CMLattice.norm_coeff_le_one_of_lt`: for
  `g ∈ 𝒪[[y]]` the series `g(ϖ z)` is integral, and `g` is integral in the degrees below `q`.

## Notation

* `q = primeNorm d p` is the norm of a prime of `K` above `p`.
* `π_p = piPrime d p` is `√-d` if `p = d` and `p` otherwise; `piPrimeInt d` is its image in `𝒪`.
* `y = taylorVia ιₚ C.translatedY` is the Taylor series at `0` of the coordinate function
  `C.translatedY`, moved to `ℂ_[p]` by the embedding `ιₚ`.
* `𝒪[[y]] = C.integralSeriesRing` is the ring of the series `g(y)` with `g` a series over `𝒪`.
* `ρ_p = varpiValuation d p` is the valuation of `π_p` divided by `q - 1`.
modules.literature:
Known result: multiplication by `π_p` on the formal group of a curve with complex multiplication is
an endomorphism in the sense of Lubin and Tate. That `b₁` is a unit follows from the bound for the
height of the formal group (`New.CMLattice.insepDegree_piPrime_le`), and the scaling is an
elementary consequence. Lubin–Tate, Formal complex multiplication in local fields.

modules.title: Doubling formulas for θ and σ and the quartic forms of doubling
modules.group: Integrality of expansions of theta functions
modules.note:
The file expresses `θ(2 z)` and `σ(2 z) ^ 2` in `θ(z)` and `σ(z)`. The quartic forms of doubling,
`doublingForms c`, are defined over any commutative ring; over `ℂ` with `c = a₁`, their values at
`(θ², σ²)` are the square of the formula for `θ(2 z)` and the formula for `σ(2 z) ^ 2`. These facts
serve to prove the cases of the theorem on Siegel units (integrality and units at torsion points)
that are used; see `Lib.CM.Integrality.TorsionValues` and `Lib.CM.Integrality.IntegralSections`.

Notions from other files:
* `C : CMLattice d`: a lattice `Λ = C.Λ` in `ℂ` with a point `t = C.t` of order two modulo `Λ`,
  scaled so that `℘''(t) = 2`, and a square root `a₁ = C.a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`.
* `C.σ`, `C.θ`: the sigma function of `Λ`, and its twisted translate by `t` normalised to `1` at
  `0`; the zeros of `θ` are the `z` with `z + t ∈ Λ`.
* `C.translatedX`: the function `x(z) = ℘(z + t) - ℘(t)`, equal to `σ² / θ²` off `t + Λ`.
* `C.twistedTranslate m y`: the translation `T_y` by `y`, twisted by the exponential factor of
  degree `m`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.doublingForms c`: the pair of quartic forms of doubling.
* `New.CMLattice.sigma_two_mul_eq`: `σ(2 z) = x' θ ^ 4` off `t + Λ`.
* `New.CMLattice.theta_two_mul`, `New.CMLattice.sigma_two_mul_sq`: `θ(2 z)` and `σ(2 z) ^ 2` as
  polynomials in `θ` and `σ`.
* `New.norm_doublingForms`: if `c` is integral and `c ^ 4 - 64` is a unit, the forms raise the
  maximum norm of a pair to the fourth power.
* `New.norm_det_eq_one_of_iterate_doublingForms`: a criterion for two pairs to reduce to distinct
  points of the projective line over the residue field.
modules.literature:
Known result: the duplication formulas for theta and sigma functions. Source: DLMF, Chapters 20 and
23.

Known result: good reduction of the duplication map on the `x`-coordinate of an elliptic curve.
Source: Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Dynamical Systems* (GTM 241, Springer, 2007), Chapters 2 and
6.

modules.title: Integrality of values of sections at torsion points
modules.group: Integrality of expansions of theta functions
modules.note:
The file defines the value `torsionValue` at a point of a function with a degree `n` (the function
value times an exponential factor that depends on `n`), which is used for sections at torsion
points, and the property `HasIntegralValues`. For a prime `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)` the file shows that `a₁`
is integral, that `max (|σ[u]|_p, |θ[u]|_p) = 1` at torsion points, and that monomials in `θ`, `σ²`
and the section `translatedYThetaCube` have integral torsion values. Here `translatedYThetaCube` is
`y θ³`, where `y` is the coordinate `translatedY` in the cubic `y² + a₁ x y = x³ + x`.

Notions from other files:
* `CMLattice d`: a lattice `Λ` with a point `t` of order two in `ℂ / Λ` and a coefficient `a₁` of
  its cubic. For `d ≠ 0` the lattice has complex multiplication by the integers of `ℚ(√-d)`.
* `σ` and `θ`: the sigma function of `Λ`, normalised so that twisted translation by a period
  multiplies it by a sign, and the theta function that vanishes exactly on `-t + Λ`.
* `twistedTranslate n v G`: the translate of a function `G` by `v`, multiplied by the exponential
  factor of `n` times the Hermitian form `H(l, z) = (π / area Λ) l̄ z`.
* `ιₚ`: the fixed embedding of `ℂ` into `ℂ_p` (`PadicPlace p`); integral means of norm at most `1`,
  that is, lying in `valRingCp p`, the set of elements of `ℂ_p` of norm at most `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.torsionValue`, `New.CMLattice.HasIntegralValues`: the torsion value `G[u]` and the
  property that all of these are integral at torsion points.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_a₁_le_one`: `a₁` is integral, because `a₁ ^ 4 - 64` is a unit.
* `New.CMLattice.torsionValue_mul`, `New.CMLattice.torsionValue_comp_isogeny`,
  `New.CMLattice.torsionValue_twistedTranslate`: the rules for products, pull-backs and translates.
* `New.CMLattice.max_norm_torsionValue`: `max (|σ[u]|_p, |θ[u]|_p) = 1` at torsion points.
* `New.CMLattice.hasIntegralValues_monomialSection`: monomials have integral torsion values.
modules.literature:
Known result: the Weber invariants of discriminant `-d` with `d ≡ 7 mod 8` are integral. Source:
Birch, *Weber's class invariants*.

Known result: the integrality of Siegel functions at torsion points. Source: Kubert and Lang,
*Modular Units*.

modules.title: The integrality principle in one variable
modules.group: Integrality of expansions of theta functions
modules.note:
* `New.CMLattice.mem_span_monomialSection`: a section with integral torsion values is an integral
  combination of monomials; `New.CMLattice.exists_polynomial_of_even` treats even sections.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_taylorVia_eq_theta_pow_mul`: its Taylor series lies in `θ ^ m 𝒪[[y]]`.

Write the section as `θ ^ m (P₀(x) + y P₁(x))`, where `P₁ = 0` if the section is even, and
interpolate at the nodes `x(tᵢ)`, where `tᵢ = t / 2 ^ i` and `i ≥ 1`. The numbers `θ[tᵢ]`, `x'(tᵢ)`
and `x(tᵢ) - x(tⱼ)` for `i ≠ j` are units.

Notions from other files:

For a lattice `Λ = C.Λ` with a point `t = C.t` of order two modulo `Λ`:
* `θ` is the normalised twisted translate of the sigma function `σ` by `t`; it vanishes on `t + Λ`.
* `x = translatedX` is `℘(z + t) - ℘(t)` and `y = translatedY` is `(℘'(z + t) - a₁ x(z)) / 2`, where
  `a₁ = C.a₁` is a constant of `C` with `‖ιₚ a₁‖ ≤ 1`; off `t + Λ`,
  `x' ^ 2 = x (4 x ^ 2 + a₁ ^ 2 x + 4)`.
* `sections m` is the space of theta functions of degree `m`; the monomial of `(a, b, c)` is
  `θ ^ (a + 2 b + 3 c) x ^ b y ^ c` off `t + Λ`, with degree
  `monomialDeg (a, b, c) = a + 2 b + 3 c`, and `spanningExponents m` is the set of triples with
  `c ≤ 1` and `a + 2 b + 3 c = m`.
* The value `G[u]` is the value at `0` of the translate of `G` by `u`, twisted by the degree `m`
  (written `torsionValue m G u`); it is called a torsion value if `u` is a torsion point, and
  `HasIntegralValues` says that all torsion values have norm at most `1` in `ℂ_p`, under the ring
  homomorphism `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` fixed by the instance `PadicPlace p`.
modules.literature:
Known result: integral expansions of theta functions of CM elliptic curves, at ordinary primes
`p ≥ 5`. Here `p` is arbitrary, but `d` is a prime congruent to `7` modulo `8`. Source: Bannai and
Kobayashi, Algebraic theta functions and the p-adic interpolation of Eisenstein-Kronecker numbers,
Duke Math. J. 153 (2010), 229-295, after Norman and Mazur–Tate.

Known result: for a lattice with complex multiplication, the value of the Siegel function at a
torsion point is a unit if two different prime ideals divide the annihilator of the point. Only the
points `t / 2 ^ i` are treated, by doubling. Source: Ramachandra and Robert; Kubert and Lang,
*Modular Units*.

modules.title: Isogenies and translates act integrally on expansions
modules.group: Integrality of expansions of theta functions
modules.note:
Let `p` be a prime and `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` a fixed embedding. For a lattice `Λ` of a `CMLattice`, the
function `y_Λ = translatedY` is the second Weierstrass coordinate at `z + t` in the model of the
lattice, `(℘′(z + t) - a₁ x(z)) / 2` with `x(z) = ℘(z + t) - ℘(t)`, `a₁` the `xy`-coefficient of
that Weierstrass model and `t` the chosen point of order two, and `translatedYThetaCube` is the
entire extension of `y θ³`, where `θ` is the theta function of degree one, normalised by `θ(0) = 1`.
The ring `integralSeriesRing` is `𝒪[[y_Λ]]`, the integral power series in the Taylor series of
`y_Λ`, and `taylorVia ιₚ f` is the Taylor series of `f` at `0` with `ιₚ` applied to its
coefficients.

* `New.CMLattice.exists_rescale_theta_eq_theta_pow_mul`: an isogeny of degree `N` pulls `θ` back to
  `θ ^ N` times an integral series in `y`.
* `New.CMLattice.rescale_translatedY_mem_integralSeriesRing`: an isogeny pulls `y` back to an
  integral series in `y`.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_le_one_of_mapsTo_lattice`: the multiplier of an isogeny is integral at `p`.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_rescale_twistedTranslate_eq_theta_pow_mul`: the pull-back of a torsion
  translate of `θ`.

The pull-back statements rest on the integrality principle for sections with integral torsion
values, and the integrality of the multiplier follows from the pull-back of `y`.
modules.literature:
Known result: an isogeny of elliptic curves with good reduction acts on the formal groups by an
integral power series. Background: Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, Chapters IV and
VII.

modules.title: The logarithm of the theta function of a CM lattice and the integral group law
modules.group: Integrality of expansions of theta functions
modules.note:
For a CM lattice, `g = -log θ` is the power series of the negative logarithm of its theta function,
read in `ℂ_p`. The file proves integrality statements for `g` and its rescalings; `expSubst f` is
the exponential series evaluated at a series `f` without constant term.

The integrality statements about the ring `𝒪[[y]]` assume that `d` is a prime congruent to `7`
modulo `8` (`PrimeSevenModEight d`). The main imported notions are the following.

* `C.θ`: the translate of the sigma function `C.σ` of the lattice `Λ` by the two-torsion point `t`,
  twisted and normalised to `θ(0) = 1`.
* `C.translatedX` and `C.translatedY`: the coordinates `x(z) = ℘(z + t) - ℘(t)` and
  `y(z) = (℘'(z + t) - a₁ x(z)) / 2` on the cubic `y² + a₁ x y = x³ + x` of the lattice; `y` is a
  parameter at the origin.
* `taylorVia ιₚ f`: the Taylor series of `f` at `0`, read in `ℂ_p` through the place `ιₚ`.
* `C.integralSeriesRing`: the ring `𝒪[[y]]` of integral power series in the series of `y`.
* `normPairClosure d`: the closure in `ℂ_p²` of the set of pairs `(α, α ᾱ)`, for integers `α` of
  `K = ℚ(√-d)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.derivative_derivative_negLogTheta`: `g'' = g''(0) + x`.
* `New.CMLattice.rescale_translatedY_mem_of_mem_normPairClosure`,
  `New.CMLattice.expSubst_sub_rescale_mem`: for a limit `(δ, s)` of pairs `(α, α ᾱ)` with `α` an
  integer of `K`, the series `y(δ z)` and `exp (s g(z) - g(δ z))` lie in `𝒪[[y]]`.
* `New.CMLattice.norm_sqrt_mul_coeff_two_negLogTheta_le_one`: `√-d g''(0)` is integral.
* `New.CMLattice.multiSeriesRing`: for linear forms `μ_i`, the ring `𝒪[[y(μ_i z)]]` of integral
  power series in the series `y(μ_i z)`.
* `New.CMLattice.translatedY_add_mem_multiSeriesRing`: the group law is integral.
modules.literature:
Known result: the second logarithmic derivative of a theta function is a Weierstrass function up to
a constant. Moreover `θ(α z) / θ(z) ^ (α ᾱ)` is a unit on the formal group.

Known result: the formal group law of a Weierstrass curve has integral coefficients. Source:
Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, IV.1 and IV.2.

modules.title: Sigma and Weierstrass functions, lattice invariants and lattices with complex multiplication
modules.group: Sigma, theta and Weierstrass functions of lattices
modules.note:
Let `L` be a period pair with lattice Λ, Weierstrass function ℘ and invariants g₂, g₃. The sigma
function `PeriodPair.σ` is built as an odd theta function for the form H(l, z) = (π/A)·l̄·z, where A
is the area of Λ; it differs from the classical sigma function by a factor exp(cz²). Its addition
formula and the description of the theta functions for twice the form give the duplication formula
of σ and the classical facts on ℘.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsAppellHumbert.theta_eq_zero_iff_mem_lattice`, `New.IsAppellHumbert.deriv_theta_ne_zero`,
  `New.IsAppellHumbert.thetaSpace_two_eq_span_pair`: a theta function f ≠ 0 for (H, χ) with
  f(0) = 0 has simple zeros exactly on Λ, and ℘f² and f² span the theta functions for (2H, χ²);
  `New.IsAppellHumbert.thetaSpace_two_eq_span` collects the three.
* `PeriodPair.σ`, `New.sigma_add_mul_sigma_sub`: for u and v outside Λ,
  σ(u + v)σ(u − v) = (℘(v) − ℘(u))σ(u)²σ(v)².
* `PeriodPair.exists_weierstrassP_eq_of_cubic`: every point of `y² = 4x³ - g₂x - g₃` is
  `(℘ z, ℘' z)`.
* `New.sigma_two_mul`: the duplication formula `σ(2z) = -℘'(z) σ(z)⁴`.
* `New.CMLattice d`: a lattice `Λ` with a point `t` of order two such that `℘''(t) = 2` and a
  square root `a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`. For `d ≠ 0` the lattice is also stable under multiplication by
  `New.quadInt d`, and neither `ω t` nor `ω̄ t` lies in it, where `ω = New.quadGen d`.
* `New.exists_lattice_eq_mul_tau`: every lattice is a(ℤτ + ℤ) with τ in the upper half plane.
* `New.g₂_eq_eisenstein`, `New.g₃_eq_eisenstein`, `New.g₂_pow_three_sub_g₃_sq_eq_discriminant`: g₂,
  g₃ and g₂³ − 27 g₃² of that lattice in terms of E₄(τ), E₆(τ) and Δ(τ).
* `New.exists_lattice_of_g₂_g₃`: conversely, every pair (a, b) with a³ − 27 b² ≠ 0 is (g₂, g₃) of a
  lattice (uniformization). The proof finds τ as a zero of a form of weight 12 that tends to 1 at
  the cusp: without a zero, its inverse would be a nonzero modular form of negative weight.

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealComplexForm.thetaSpace` Λ B χ: the entire f with f(z + l) = χ(l)·exp(B(l, z) + B(l,
  l)/2)·f(z) for l ∈ Λ. A `New.ThetaTori.LatticeForm Λ` is a form B that carries Λ in its type.
* `New.RealComplexForm.riemannForm`: the Riemann form of B, E(u, v) = Im(B(u, v) − B(v, u))/(2π).
* `New.IsAppellHumbert`: Appell–Humbert data: Re B is symmetric, and on Λ one has |χ| = 1 and
  χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi E(m, l)).
modules.literature:
Known result: Sigma and theta functions of a lattice, their addition and doubling formulas, and
uniformisation. Here sigma is the odd section of a canonical factor of automorphy rather than a
product, and the origin is moved to a point of order two. Uniformisation comes from the vanishing of
modular forms of negative weight. Source: J. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, VI, and
Advanced Topics (1994), I.5; A. Weil, Elliptic Functions according to Eisenstein and Kronecker
(1976); for uniformisation, A. Sutherland, 18.783 Lecture 15 (2023), Cor. 15.12.

modules.title: Theta functions of a CM elliptic curve: Weierstrass equation and spanning monomials
modules.group: Sigma, theta and Weierstrass functions of lattices
modules.note:
Let `C : New.CMLattice d` be a CM datum with lattice Λ, point t of order two and constant a₁. Let
H(l, z) = π l̄ z / area(Λ), and let σ be the sigma function of Λ. Let θ be the twisted translate of
σ by t with θ(0) = 1 and multiplier χ = `New.CMLattice.multiplier`. Write x(z) = ℘(z + t) − ℘(t),
y(z) = ½(℘′(z + t) − a₁x(z)) and G = `New.CMLattice.translatedYThetaCube`; `New.CMLattice.sections`
m is the space of theta functions for Λ, the form mH and χ^m. The file proves an addition formula
for θ and the Weierstrass equation for x, y and for σ², θ, G, shows that the monomials θ^a σ^{2b}
G^c with c ≤ 1 span the sections of each degree, and transfers the identities to the Taylor series
of x and y at 0.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.CMLattice.theta_add_mul_theta_sub`, `New.CMLattice.theta_sq`: the addition formula for
  θ(z + w)θ(z − w) with z off t + Λ, and θ² = (℘ − ℘(t))σ² off Λ.
* `New.CMLattice.deriv_translatedX_sq`, `New.CMLattice.weierstrass_equation`,
  `New.CMLattice.deriv_translatedY_eq`: off t + Λ, x′² = x(4x² + a₁²x + 4), y² + a₁xy = x³ + x and
  y′ = 1 + 3x² − a₁y.
* `New.CMLattice.translatedYThetaCube_sq_add`: G² + a₁σ²θG = σ⁶ + σ²θ⁴ everywhere.
* `New.CMLattice.comp_mul_mem_sections`, `New.CMLattice.twistedTranslate_comp_mem`: for d a
  prime ≡ 7 mod 8, sections pull back along isogenies z ↦ az, and z ↦ (T_uθ)(δ̄z) is a section of
  degree N when z ↦ δ̄z is a degree-N isogeny of C to itself and δu lies in Λ.
* `New.CMLattice.exists_mul_eq_of_mem_sections`: division by a section z ↦ (T_uθ)(az) with a ≠ 0,
  where T_u = `D.twistedTranslate 1 u` and θ belong to a CM datum D. The zeros of such a section are
  simple (`New.CMLattice.deriv_twistedTranslate_theta_comp_mul_ne_zero`).
* `New.CMLattice.monomialDeg`, `New.CMLattice.monomialSection`: the degree a + 2b + 3c of a triple
  (a, b, c) and the monomial θ^a σ^{2b} G^c.
* `New.CMLattice.sections_le_span_monomialSection`: the monomials with c ≤ 1, a + 2b + 3c = m (the
  triples in `New.CMLattice.spanningExponents` m) span the sections of degree m.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMLattice`: A lattice `Λ` stable under the integers of `ℚ(√-d)`, with a point `t` of order
  two modulo `Λ` such that `ω t`, `ω̄ t ∉ Λ` for `ω = (1 + √-d) / 2`, scaled so that `℘''(t) = 2`,
  and a square root `a₁` of `12 ℘(t)`. The conditions on `ℚ(√-d)` and `ω` are void for `d = 0`.
* `PeriodPair.σ`: the sigma function of the lattice, a chosen odd theta function for the form H and
  the multiplier `New.sigmaSign`, with derivative 1 at 0.
* `New.sigmaSign`: The multiplier of σ: 1 at w if w/2 lies in Λ, and −1 otherwise.
* `New.IsAppellHumbert` B χ, for a form B on a lattice L: Re B is symmetric, and on L one has
  |χ| = 1 and χ(l + m) = χ(l)χ(m)·exp(πi E(m, l)), E the Riemann form of B.
* `New.CMLattice.translatedYThetaCube`: The entire function G = σ·(σ′θ − σ·(θ′ + ½a₁θ)), written as
  a pointwise product of functions.
modules.literature:
Known results: sigma and theta functions of a lattice, their addition formulas, the Weierstrass
equation and the elliptic functions with poles at one point are classical. See `Lib.CM.Sigma.Basic`
for the sigma function used here and for sources.
